minutes.headline: Commission approved an alum treatment at Hemlock Beach and the Flat Hill Road bridge, and re-elected its officers; a Howard Street driveway was continued.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission reviewed two draft forest cutting plans with the town forester, approved a field change for an alum treatment at Hemlock Beach, and acted on several wetlands hearings. The 250 Howard Street driveway hearing was continued for a tree count and denser plantings, and the Flat Hill Road bridge replacement was approved. Officers were elected, and the board discussed the 40B project at Howard Street.

what_happened.line: The commission approved a field change to the Hickory Hills order of conditions for an alum treatment at Hemlock Beach, with phosphate testing before and after.
The Flat Hill Road bridge replacement notice of intent was approved.
The 250 Howard Street driveway hearing was continued to the 21st; the applicant is to bring a tree count, tree plan and planting density statement.
The town forester was sent back to revise the Hollis Road and Chase Road draft cutting plans, with the Hollis Road plan to return at the next meeting.
Bob Pease was elected chairman, Richard Bursch vice chairman and Jeff Viviano clerk.

why_it_matters: The alum treatment at Hemlock Beach and the Flat Hill Road bridge work affect a swimming area and a road crossing, and the commission put conditions on the first, including water testing.
The Howard Street driveway crosses wetlands in an area of critical environmental concern, and the commission has not decided it, so the tree and planting plans due on the 21st will shape the outcome.
The forester said the two cutting-plan parcels should bring in timber revenue, so the projects are not a net cost, but the plans were sent back for revision before any work is approved.
watch_next: The commission's meeting on the 21st, when the 250 Howard Street, Highland Street, Pleasant Street, Flynn Road and Rue Street hearings return, along with the revised cutting plans and the lake association's treatment report.
A public hearing the chair intends to schedule on amending the Table Rock and Lane land use plans to remove the bow hunting permit requirement.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the substantive votes: the alum treatment, both negative determinations, the Fire Road 12, Reservoir Road, Beal Street and bridge approvals, the three officer elections, and the survey. They differ mainly because the official minutes omit five continuance votes and several decisions our recording captured, and our captions garble a few names and places.
